summary: Milestone A · Integrations dashboard verification — INDEPENDENT PASS. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_milestone_a_integrations.py (23 tests, 100% pass). Also re-ran /app/backend/tests/test_security_invariants.py (35/35 pass, includes the new 5 integrations tests). Frontend Admin Integrations tab exercised end-to-end for BOTH admin and support roles via Playwright; all 14 rows visible, correct status pills, detail modal opens, admin can Test/Disable, support gets read-only (disabled buttons + 403 on write endpoints). Regression spot-checks green: cookie auth flow, billing/checkout (Stripe test-mode URL returned), privacy export (no password_hash / bcrypt marker), admin user detail (sealed mask literal '•••• (sealed)' present). Actual runtime slugs discovered: stripe, google_auth, email_password, resend, sendgrid, twilio, openai, anthropic, gemini, elevenlabs, media_storage, razorpay, paypal, paystack. The review request mentioned 'google_oauth (or google)' — actual slug is `google_auth` (documentation should be aligned).

minor.issue: Returns 403 instead of the mandated 401 for anonymous callers. Both semantically deny access (no auth). If the spec strictly requires 401 for missing bearer/cookie versus 403 for insufficient role, add an explicit no-token branch in the auth dependency that raises 401 before role check. Non-blocking — access is still refused.

The mandate listed the Google Auth provider as `google_oauth` (or `google`); the running registry exposes it as `google_auth`. Fix is docs-only, not code — either update the spec to say `google_auth` or rename the adapter slug (breaks the DB integration_configs snapshot if renamed).

integration_issues.flow: Admin · Integrations tab · Disable→Enable on resend
integration_issues.issue: Playwright observed that after clicking Disable, the status pill did not update to DISABLED before the next assertion — likely a stale render race between the flash banner mount and the subsequent load() refetch. Backend disable/enable is verified correct via pytest (test_disable_then_enable_reverts_status). If the UX needs guaranteed pill-refresh, consider optimistically setting the row status to DISABLED on click before awaiting the round-trip, or await load() in the toggle handler with a spinner block on the row. Not a blocker.

action_items: Docs alignment: update the founder-mandate spec / registry inventory doc to use slug `google_auth` (not `google_oauth` / `google`) so downstream automation aligns to the live registry.

Optional: return 401 (not 403) from the admin-integrations router when no auth is presented, to match the review-request contract exactly. Requires a small change to get_current_user or an equivalent dependency to distinguish missing-credential vs insufficient-role.

Optional UX polish: eager-update the row's status pill on Disable/Enable click so the transition to DISABLED is visible immediately (current implementation depends on the subsequent load() refetch, which may look stale for one paint).
critical_code_review_comments: integrations/registry.py `_try` swallows import failures silently — good for resilience, but the admin dashboard has NO surface for 'adapter failed to load'. If a future adapter throws at import time it disappears from the 14-count with no operator signal. Consider recording a failed-load synthetic row (slug=<module>, status=DEGRADED, note=import_error).

integrations/base.py:status() returns CONNECTED as the final else — this is the only path where a provider claims full production health WITHOUT any positive success signal, purely because validate_configuration().is_test_mode is false and there are no recent errors. `email_password` today reports CONNECTED with `is_test_mode=False` and no recent success recorded; that's fine for a self-contained bcrypt provider, but for future outbound integrations you probably want to require _last_success_at > 0 (or first_boot=True) before promoting past TEST_MODE.

routers/integrations.py — the write endpoints (test/enable/disable) do NOT require CSRF for cookie-auth clients. In this codebase, cookie sessions are cross-verified with X-CSRF-Token on other state-changing paths. Bearer JWT is exempt from CSRF, so pytest is fine, but a browser session (which the admin dashboard actually uses) will bypass the double-submit token. Recommend adding csrf_dependency() to POST /test|/enable|/disable to match /api/v1/billing/checkout and /api/v1/users/me/change-password.

routers/integrations.py::enable_integration reverts _disabled=False but the status will re-derive from validate_configuration() — this is correct, but there is no user-facing signal of WHICH prior status was restored. The response returns the new status via `p.status().value`, which is fine, but persisting the pre-disable status snapshot would be more auditable.

integrations/health.py::snapshot_provider is called after every describe/test/enable/disable — that is 1 mongo upsert per admin request. Fine at v0.1 volume, but consider debouncing (last snapshot < 30s ago → skip) if the admin dashboard is left open with auto-refresh in a future milestone.

Frontend Admin.jsx::IntegrationsTab — the Test/Disable buttons for support role receive `disabled={!isAdmin}` which produces HTML `disabled=""` (truthy). Playwright observed this correctly. However the button still has the same visual style as an enabled disabled=false button (only opacity-40 via Tailwind); an aria-disabled attribute plus title tooltip explaining 'admin only' would improve accessibility.
